Accepts any JSON value, including a top-level number, string, boolean or null. Rejects comments, trailing commas, non-JSON numbers, duplicate decoded keys and unpaired Unicode surrogates. Duplicate-key and Unicode checks are deliberate interoperability rules. JSON only: not JavaScript, CSS, XML or HTML.

Key order, number spelling and string escape spelling are preserved. Numbers are not converted to floating point, so large numbers and exponents are not rounded. Pretty-print and Minify change only insignificant whitespace. Source text is never executed or sent to a server.

Limits: 64,000 input UTF-16 code units, 64 nested containers, 20,000 tokens and 256,000 formatted-output code units. Limit errors are reported without truncation; output-size errors point to the start of the document rather than a syntax fault.

Source code and structured text can contain secrets and private information. Automatic history and remembered results are off by default. Manual saves or enabling them can store source and output locally. Sharing sends the reviewed result to the app you choose.
Explicit imports restore inputs only; press Run. Remember results, if enabled, can reconstruct the last successful result. Saved modes retain only the operation and indentation.
Source or output exceeds local history and saved-result limits. It will not be retained there; you can still copy or share the full result.
